title: Conversation memory versus the system of record

concept.heading: Memory is short, scoped, allow-listed, and never a second copy of the CRM
paragraphs: Across a few turns an assistant should remember which donor the staff member means, what they asked for, and the approval id that is pending. It should not remember a donor's email, their giving total, or anything a staff member could later read back as if it were true. The CRM is the system of record; memory is a sticky note, and sticky notes expire.

Four rules make that real in code. A TTL: every entry carries expires_at and recall ignores the rest. A scope: entries are keyed by conversation, so one staff member's context never bleeds into another's. An allow-list: remember() refuses any key that is not a conversational one, so a well-meaning prompt cannot turn memory into a shadow database. And isolation: this module never calls the CRM, which the check proves by counting rows before and after.
When memory and the CRM disagree, the CRM wins and the entry is discarded. Build that into how tools use memory: a remembered donor id is a hint to look the donor up, never a fact to act on.
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: Global variables in a Copilot Studio topic, scoped to the session, versus the Dataverse table. You already knew not to copy the table into variables; here that rule is enforced by the code.

pythonBlock.title: Python you need: UPSERT in SQLite, frozenset membership, injected time
pythonBlock.intro: ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE makes remember an upsert. time.time is a parameter so the check can age entries instantly.

spec: Implement ConversationMemory per the stub: remember (upsert with TTL, allow-listed keys), recall (unexpired only), forget, forget_expired.
Add two tools: remember_context(conversation_id, key, value) and recall_context(conversation_id), both requiring donors:read; MemoryPolicyError becomes an invalid_arguments error result.
Have the loop or agent pass a conversation id so a staff member's context survives a few turns and disappears after 30 minutes.
Write, in the module docstring, the one-sentence rule for a client: where the truth lives, and what happens when memory disagrees.
askClaudeFor: A review of the allow-list: is there a key you want to add that is actually a system-of-record fact in disguise?
How a host could pass a conversation id to an MCP tool (hint: a parameter the host fills, or _meta).
writeYourself: remember and recall, including the policy check and the TTL comparison.
The two tools and their scope checks.

check.command: uv run --directory middleware python checks/run.py m5-2-memory-vs-record
check.summary: Entries are per conversation and upsert; expired entries vanish on recall and forget_expired; system-of-record keys raise MemoryPolicyError; the CRM's donors and receipts are byte-for-byte unchanged by memory writes.
